title: Clarify model-intake triage attributes and pinning guidance for community model onboarding
creator: Ava Chen
description: This ticket clarifies the intake triage attributes, minimum profiling requirements, and the recommended pinning and soft-fallback guidance for new community/open models submitted to the Redwood model catalog. It consolidates PRD notes and edge-case decisions from recent intake reviews so that on-call reviewers and automated gates have an unambiguous checklist to accept, soft-pin, or reject a variant.
background: During Q1 onboarding of three community models we observed inconsistent reviewer decisions on when to require hard version pinning vs soft pin + auto-fallback. In several cases runtime regressions reached production because compatibility signals were missing from the intake. This task defines a small, prescriptive set of attributes and acceptance criteria to reduce decision drift and support automation of the admission gate.
goals: Define a minimal profiling bundle that intake engineers must collect for every new open model submission
Standardize the compatibility signals and categories used by runtime and catalog services
Provide clear rules for hard pin, soft pin with monitoring, and disallow lists
Create acceptance criteria and examples so automated admission checks can be implemented
Update the catalog ingestion schema and reviewer UI to surface required fields
non_goals: Redesign runtime scheduling or kernel selection logic
Complete automation of rollbacks; this ticket only defines signals and reviewer UI changes
requirements: Intake profiling: each submission must include runtime profile artifacts for the model at three sequence lengths (64, 512, 2048) run on our standard reference hardware; lightweight traces that include peak memory, median latency per token, and KV cache behavior are acceptable
Compatibility signals: intake must provide model_architecture, tokenizer_family, kv_cache_compatible (true|false), fp_format (fp16|int8|int4), and expected_max_ctx_size

Pinning guidance: rule-based mapping from compatibility signals to pinning recommendation: hard_pin required when kv_cache_compatible=false OR architecture mismatch with our optimized kernels; soft_pin when kv_cache_compatible=true but fp_format is a non-default quantization and runtime hasn't validated it
Fallback policy: every non-hard-pinned model must register at least one compatible fallback variant and a default fallback route in the catalog entry
Reviewer UI: reviewer must see a summarized compatibility score (0-100), profiling artifacts links, and checkboxes for accept / soft_pin / hard_pin / request_more_info
API schema: catalog ingestion endpoint must accept new optional fields: profiling_artifact_url, compatibility_signals, recommended_pin_type, fallback_variants
Audit trail: every intake decision saved with reviewer comments and linked to the runtime validation run ID
acceptance_criteria: A PR for catalog ingestion schema change merged and deployed to staging that includes the new fields and validation rules
Reviewer UI mock implemented and reviewed by Design and Eng (link to Figma in comments)
Onboarding playbook updated with the minimal profiling run commands and example artifacts
Automated admission check (validation job) fails submissions missing profiling artifacts or required compatibility signals
At least two recent incoming community model submissions are reprocessed by the staging pipeline and receive consistent pin recommendations
Documentation for runtime teams describing how compatibility signals map to runtime scheduling decisions is published
ui_changes: Add a compact compatibility panel to the model intake reviewer page: displays compatibility_score, key signals, a link to profiling artifact bundle, and recommended pin action. Include a free-text reviewer rationale field and buttons that set the catalog entry pin status. Work with Design for placement and copy; Figma link in comments.
api_changes: catalog POST/PUT accepts new top-level fields: profiling_artifact_url (string), compatibility_signals (stringified JSON accepted for now), recommended_pin_type (hard|soft|none), fallback_variants (comma-separated list). Ingest validation rejects requests without minimal profiling when 'community' origin is set.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): implement schema + validation, hook UI mock, and run reprocessing on queued submissions. Phase 2 (canary): enable automated admission checks for 10% of new community submissions and require reviewer confirmation. Phase 3 (GA): require profiling bundle for all community model entries and enforce recommended pin type automatically for soft_pin cases unless reviewer overrides.
risks: Uptake friction: community submitters may fail to produce the profiling bundle, increasing reviewer workload
False negatives: profiling on our reference hardware may not capture edge-case regressions on customer hardware
Schema churn: accepting stringified JSON for compatibility_signals is a temporary compromise and may cause parsing errors across clients
Operational: automated admission checks blocking valid submissions if validation is too strict
decisions: Adopt a small mandatory profiling bundle at sequence lengths 64/512/2048 instead of full benchmark runs to reduce submitter burden
Use a three-tier pin recommendation: hard|soft|none with explicit fallback variant requirement for soft/none
Compatibility_score is a derived helper for reviewers only and will not be used directly by runtime routing in phase 1
Store audit records in the catalog DB and mirror to the central audit log as part of the SEC-219 integration
open_questions: What exact format should profiling_artifact_url point to (zip vs directory vs artifact id)? Proposal: artifact id referencing internal storage for now
Should we require an automated runtime quick-check for every soft_pin submission before GA? (Engineering preference: yes, but cost needs approval)
Can we accept 2 sequence lengths for very large models to reduce cost? (trade-off between coverage and burden)
How will external contributors authenticate to upload profiling artifacts? (work with infra and OSS intake)
